record.paper_title: Modeling social resilience: Questions, answers, open problems
record.original_question: What should be the focus of organizational resilience when resilience is modeled as an emergent systemic property of a collective rather than as an individual trait? The question includes why some organizations can maintain or enhance capabilities under crisis while others fail.

evidence.quote: Questions • What is the focus of organizational resilience?
resilience is generally seen as ‘the ability of groups or communities to cope with external stresses and disturbances as a result of social, political and environmental change’
It is an open question why and how some organizations manage to thrive and enhance core capabilities when faced with a crisis, while others fail

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an organization modeled as a collective system consisting of a set of agents A = {a_1, ..., a_n} together with an interaction network G = (A, E) describing their working relations, a vector of capabilities C(t) ∈ R^k that the organization possesses at time t (e.g., production, coordination, knowledge-processing capacities), and a stochastic crisis process X(t) that acts as an external stress, perturbing both the network G and the agents' states. Suppose that resilience is not a property of any individual agent but an emergent property of the collective, defined formally as a functional R[A, G, C, X] that measures the ability of the system to maintain or increase its capability vector C(t) after the onset of a crisis X(t).

(a) Propose a precise mathematical definition of the functional R[A, G, C, X] (the "focus" of organizational resilience) that captures the emergent, system-level nature of resilience rather than aggregating individual traits.

(b) Within this framework, identify structural conditions on (A, G, C) — for instance, on network topology, redundancy, modularity, feedback loops, or adaptive rules governing the evolution of G and C under X — that are necessary and/or sufficient for the organization to satisfy R[A, G, C, X] ≥ R(0), i.e., to maintain or enhance its capabilities under the crisis process.

(c) Characterize, in this formalism, why two organizations with identical initial capability vectors C(0) but different (A, G) can exhibit qualitatively different outcomes under the same crisis process X — one thriving and one failing — and produce a rigorous criterion separating the two regimes.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open modeling problem about how to define and analyze organizational resilience as an emergent collective property. No general mathematical theory resolving (a)–(c) has been established; the literature offers various qualitative frameworks and case studies but no agreed formal definition or structural characterization, so the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Modeling social resilience: Questions, answers, open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses organizational resilience as an open question regarding why some organizations thrive while others fail under crisis.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of defining and characterizing organizational resilience as an emergent systemic property is presented as open.
